# 2 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Seven brothers were arrested together with their mother. The king tried to break them with whips and leather cords, trying to force them to eat pork in violation of the law.

**2** One of them stepped forward and spoke for all of them: "What are you trying to find out by doing this to us? We are ready to die before we will betray the laws of our fathers."

**3** The king exploded with fury. He ordered iron pans and cauldrons to be heated.

**4** They were heated at once. He commanded his men to cut out the tongue of the one who had spoken, scalp him, and cut off his hands and feet — all of this while the brothers and the mother watched.

**5** When the man was completely destroyed, the king ordered him brought to the fire still alive, still breathing, and fried in the pan. The smoke rolled up and spread through the room. The brothers and their mother looked at one another and strengthened each other for noble death, saying:

**6** "The LORD God sees this. He truly has compassion on us, just as Moses testified against the people to their faces in his song: 'And he will have compassion on his servants.'"

**7** When the first brother had died, they dragged out the second for the king's amusement. They tore the scalp from his head, hair and all, and demanded: "Eat — or we will take apart your body, piece by piece."

**8** He answered them in the language of his ancestors. The word was: "Never." And so they did to him what they had done to the first.

**9** As his breath was leaving him, he said: "You are sending us out of this life, you monster. But the King of the universe will raise us up to a life renewed forever — because we are dying for his laws."

**10** They brought out the third for their sport. When they commanded it, he stuck out his tongue without hesitation. He stretched out his hands without flinching.

**11** "These came to me from Heaven," he said calmly. "For the sake of his laws I hold them cheap. And from him I expect to get them back."

**12** The king and his court stared at the young man in disbelief. He simply did not seem to feel what was happening to him.

**13** They killed him. They brought out the fourth and worked on him the same way.

**14** As he was dying, he said: "Better to be killed by human hands and hold onto the hope that God himself will raise us up. For you — there is no resurrection. None."

**15** They brought the fifth and tortured him.

**16** He stared at the king and said: "You have power over human beings because you are a man among men. Do with us what you like. But don't make the mistake of thinking God has abandoned his people.

**17** Keep watching. You'll see just how tremendous his power is when he brings his torment down on you and on your children."

**18** When they brought the sixth, he was already near death when he spoke: "Don't fool yourself. We are suffering because of our own sins against our God — we know that, and it is astonishing and right.

**19** But you — fighting against God? You will not walk away from that unpunished. Not you."

**20** Through all of this the mother was extraordinary. She deserves to be remembered forever. She watched all seven of her sons die in a single day — and she endured it with courage because she hoped in the LORD.

**21** She spoke to each of them in the language of their ancestors. Filled with a spirit of exaltation, she charged her woman's tenderness with a man's courage and said:

**22** "I do not know how life appeared in my womb. I did not give you breath or life. I did not compose from nothing the elements that make up each of you.

**23** Therefore the one who created the world — who shaped humanity's first form and ordained how all things would come to be — in his mercy, he will give you back your life and your breath. Because you are now giving up those lives for his laws."

**24** Antiochus was humiliated by all this. He suspected — rightly — that the words of the sons were a rebuke directed at him. The youngest was still alive, so Antiochus changed tactics. He spoke to the boy personally. He made solemn promises: enormous wealth, a life of privilege, a place among the king's Friends, a future in public service — if only the boy would abandon the ways of his fathers.

**25** The boy would not hear a word of it. So the king turned to the mother. He urged her to persuade her last son to save himself.

**26** She took some convincing. But eventually she agreed to speak with him.

**27** She leaned in close and whispered to him in their own language — and what she said was the opposite of what the tyrant expected. "My son," she said, "have pity on me. I carried you nine months in my body. I nursed you for three years. I have raised you and brought you to where you stand. Look at me.

**28** I beg you, my child — look at the sky. Look at the earth. Look at everything in them. Understand this: God did not make any of it from things that already existed. And that is how human beings came to exist too.

**29** Don't be afraid of this butcher. Show yourself worthy of your brothers. Take death. And then God in his mercy will give you back to me — you and your brothers together."

**30** She was still speaking when the boy turned to the king: "What are you waiting for? I will not obey the king's command. I obey the law that was given to our fathers through Moses.

**31** As for you — you who have invented every conceivable evil to use against the Hebrew people — you will not escape the hands of God. Not now, not ever.

**32** We are suffering for our own sins, yes.

**33** Our living LORD is angry with us for a time, to correct and discipline us. But he will be reconciled with his servants again.

**34** But you — you wretched, filthy man, the lowest creature breathing — don't swagger about, don't let yourself be inflated by hollow hopes, when you raise your hand against the servants of God.

**35** You have not escaped the judgment of the almighty, all-seeing God. Not yet.

**36** My brothers bore brief suffering and have now passed into everlasting life under God's covenant. But you, by God's verdict, will get exactly the punishment your arrogance deserves.

**37** Like my brothers, I give my body and my life for the laws of our fathers. I call on God: let him act quickly to show mercy to our nation. Through suffering and plagues let him bring you to confess that he alone is God,

**38** and through me and my brothers may he bring to an end the righteous anger of the Almighty that has fallen on our whole people."

**39** The king's rage boiled over. He treated the seventh brother more savagely than the rest — contempt was something Antiochus could not bear.

**40** So the boy died too, pure to the last, with absolute trust in the LORD.

**41** After her sons, the mother died.

**42** That is enough concerning the sacrificial meals and the inhuman tortures.
